metadata.title: Taste Is All You Need
metadata.purpose: Show viewers how to access Claude Design, run three quick workflows, and apply an advanced Cowork-to-Design pipeline for on-brand output.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: Taste Is All You Need?

beats.narration_text: Merhaba. This is Liam, in for Bear. What if you could go from an empty folder to a shippable design in under an hour? Claude Design makes that real — and today I will show you exactly how.

props.ask: What is Claude Design and how do I access it?
props.answer_preview: Claude Design is a separate product at claude.ai/design that...
props.command: What if you could go from an empty folder to a shippable design in under an hour?

beats.narration_text: Claude Design is a separate product. It does not live inside the regular Claude app. Its own URL is claude dot ai slash design. It runs on Opus 4.7 — the best vision model Anthropic has shipped. You need a Pro or Max plan to access it.

card.sub: claude.ai/design — Pro or Max plan required

beats.narration_text: Three quick tests to try first. One: go to Wireframe, select High Fidelity, paste a two-line prompt — you get a full website. Two: go to Slide Deck, prompt a pitch, answer Claude's questions — full deck in one shot. Three: pick From Template, describe a visual story — you get a fully animated video with motion and transitions.

illustration.concept: Three workflow paths in Claude Design
illustration.layout: Three vertical columns labeled '1 Website', '2 Slide Deck', '3 Animated Video'. Each column shows a simple icon at top (browser, slides, play button) with a two-step arrow: Prompt → Output. Terracotta connector lines between steps.

beats.narration_text: Here is the advanced workflow. Start in Cowork. Drop every brand asset — logos, slides, photos, landing pages — into one folder. Open Cowork, select the folder, and prompt it to extract a DESIGN dot MD file. That is your brand guideline in a format Claude Design can actually read.

card.sub: Extract brand guidelines from any folder of assets

beats.narration_text: Then go to claude dot ai slash design. Upload DESIGN dot MD as context. Every future prompt applies it automatically. You never re-specify colors or fonts again. Good prompt structure: goal, layout, content, constraints — four inputs locked in. When the design system is uploaded and the prompt is specific, Claude Design shines.

card.sub: DESIGN.md = auto brand context for every generation

beats.narration_text: There is a free website called getdesign dot md. You can download the brand guidelines for nearly any company — Mastercard, Airbnb, Ferrari — and hand them directly to Claude Design. It copies the style instantly. The AI does ten designs. Your job is to pick one.

card.sub: getdesign.md → paste → generate in that style

beats.narration_text: Go to claude dot ai slash design right now. Open a new project. Upload any brand asset you have — or grab one from getdesign dot md. Run your first prompt. See what comes back. Then decide which one to ship.

card.sub: Upload a brand asset and run your first generation

beats.narration_text: Taste is all you need. Claude Design builds ten dashboards in ten minutes. What it cannot do is tell you which one to ship for your specific users at this specific moment. That is taste. And taste just got more expensive. This is Liam, in for Bear.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you're using Claude to generate design assets and you're getting technically correct but aesthetically wrong output. Ask Claude to show you the taste-transfer method: how to describe your aesthetic preferences in a way Claude can operationalize, what reference examples to include, and how to give feedback on a design that lands without a design vocabulary.

props.command: I'm using Claude to generate design assets and I'm getting technically correct but aesthetically wrong output — it looks like a template, not my taste. Show me the taste-transfer method: how to describe my aesthetic preferences in a way Claude can operationalize, what reference examples to include, and how to give feedback on a design that lands without a professional design vocabulary.
Take what you learned from [Taste Is All You Need] and apply it to your own work. What's one thing you'll try first?
props.runningText: paste this into Claude and run it on your own work…
